newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb's money system in rebel enclave by January.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb's money system in rebel enclave by January.

text.p: Croatia's currency and payment system would be fully established in the country's last Serb-held enclave of Eastern Slavonia by mid January, an official said on Monday.

National news agency HINA quoted Ivan Majdak, head of a state coordination body of public enterprises, as saying the National Bank of Croatia pledged to have the payment system in the enclave operational by January 15.
It did not give more details.

Eastern Slavonia, monitored by some 5,000 peacekeepers, is due to return to Zagreb's rule some time next year. The current means of payment in the fertile, oil-rich enclave are Yugoslav dinar, Croatian kuna and German mark.
Agriculture firms in the enclave have agreed to deliver lists of assets and employees to Zagreb, "to speed up their integration into Croatian economic system," Majdak said.
